## Explore the Seven Summits

```{r summit-map, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
summits <- data.frame(
  mountain = c("Mount Everest", "Aconcagua", "Denali", "Kilimanjaro",
               "Mount Elbrus", "Vinson Massif", "Puncak Jaya"),
  continent = c("Asia", "South America", "North America", "Africa",
                "Europe", "Antarctica", "Oceania"),
  location = c("Nepal / China", "Argentina", "Alaska, United States", "Tanzania",
               "Russia", "Ellsworth Mountains, Antarctica", "Central Papua, Indonesia"),
  elevation_m = c(8848.86, 6961, 6190, 5895, 5642, 4892, 4884),
  latitude = c(27.9881, -32.6532, 63.0695, -3.0674, 43.3499, -78.5255, -4.0788),
  longitude = c(86.9250, -70.0109, -151.0074, 37.3556, 42.4453, -85.6171, 137.1583),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

summits$popup <- sprintf(
  "<div style='line-height:1.6'><b style='font-size:17px'>%s</b><br>%s<br><b>Elevation: %s m</b></div>",
  htmlEscape(summits$mountain),
  htmlEscape(summits$location),
  format(summits$elevation_m, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
)

atlas <- leaflet(options = leafletOptions(minZoom = 1, worldCopyJump = TRUE),
                 height = 575) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron, group = "Light atlas") %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery, group = "Satellite imagery") %>%
  setView(lng = 14, lat = 18, zoom = 2)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(summits))) {
  point <- summits[i, ]
  atlas <- atlas %>%
    addCircleMarkers(
      lng = point$longitude, lat = point$latitude,
      radius = 9, color = "#17303B", weight = 2, stroke = TRUE,
      fillColor = "#EDB269", fillOpacity = 1,
      label = point$mountain,
      popup = HTML(point$popup),
      group = point$continent
    )
}

atlas <- atlas %>%
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = c("Light atlas", "Satellite imagery"),
    overlayGroups = unique(summits$continent),
    position = "topright",
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = TRUE)
  )

atlas
```

<div class="note">
<strong>How to interact:</strong> Click a summit marker for a popup. Use your mouse or touch controls to pan and zoom. In the upper-right corner, select satellite imagery or toggle continents on and off.<br><br>
<strong>Geographic note:</strong> This project uses the Messner Seven Summits list, which includes Puncak Jaya for Oceania rather than Mount Kosciuszko. Summit coordinates and elevations are approximate reference values.<br><br>
<strong>Created:</strong> October 17, 2026. <strong>Technology:</strong> R Markdown + R <code>leaflet</code> package + OpenStreetMap/CARTO/Esri tiles.
</div>
